title: Studies on the variability of the uptake and effect of drugs and endogenous substances in blood cells
summary: In this study, we are investigating the variability of the uptake and effect of endogenous substances in blood cells (red and white blood cells, platelets). Many drugs and the active substances they contain require specialized proteins in the cell membrane (outer boundary of the body's cells) - so-called membrane transporters - in order to be absorbed into the body's cells. In organs such as the intestine or liver, these transporters have already been well studied and have helped to improve our understanding of drug uptake. In contrast, the transport of active substances into cellular blood components has not yet been sufficiently investigated. The same transporters are often also involved in the uptake of endogenous substances such as serotonin. The aim of this research project is therefore to investigate drug transporters in these cells in more detail.

interventions.name: A maximum of 60 mL of blood is taken once from the healthy volunteers (venous blood sampling).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Caucasian
2) Written declaration of consent signed and available
Exclusion criteria:
1) known diseases of the hematopoietic system (e.g. blood clotting disorders, vascular diseases, neoplasia of the hematopoietic system)
2) known diseases of the hematopoietic system in 1st degree relatives
3) medication taken within the last week (except oral contraceptives)
4) Blood donation in the last 8 weeks
5) Pregnancy and breastfeeding
6) Known infectious diseases (e.g. hepatitis, HIV)
7) Persons in an active dependent relationship with the study leaders
